content: Patell Z assumes homoskedasticity (constant variance estimation to event window); fails under event-induced volatility — over-rejects. BMP self-adjusts via cross-sectional denominator. Kolari-Pynnonen correction needed when >30% of events share a calendar date (cross-sectional correlation). Corrado rank test best for single-day non-normal returns but loses power over multi-day CARs. Generalized Rank T (KP 2011) is most robust: handles cross-sectional and serial correlation plus event-induced volatility simultaneously. Standard sign test uses p=0.5 baseline; Cowan (1992) generalized sign test uses empirical estimation-window positive fraction — required under non-zero drift.
